A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M4Human and RT-Mesh, with matching core experiments. All supplied pages, figures, tables, and equations are readable. v1 ends after the references; v3 includes supplementary Sections 7–11.

before.justification: v1 reports original HMR comparisons, dataset-scale experiments, multimodal fusion results, and downstream action-recognition results in Tables 2–4 and Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds detailed benchmark scores, action- and distance-dependent errors, qualitative comparisons, and data-loading measurements.

M1.justification: The four-frame input, two-stage BEV localization and local 3D reconstruction, SMPL-X outputs, and feature-concatenation fusion remain. The supplement specifies architecture, losses, and data-loading implementation without establishing a revised HMR algorithm.

E1.justification: Demonstrated coverage remains the same 661K-frame, 20-subject, 50-action dataset, evaluated for HMR and HAR. The new action/distance analyses subdivide existing coverage. v3 claims motion-prediction evaluation, but supplies no corresponding protocol or results establishing an additional evaluated task.

E2.justification: The HMR comparators remain mmMesh, P4Transformer, RT-Pose, RETR, and TokenHMR; HAR retains CNN, AGCN, and BlockGCN. Supplementary Table 6 expands reporting for existing methods, without adding a competing HMR model.

E3.justification: New analyses evaluate errors by individual action and sensing distance, and Section 8 reports a single-GPU, single-process loading-time comparison. The original splits, action-group protocols, and HMR metrics remain. Newly specified training budgets do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds per-action error distributions, distance sensitivity, HAR confusion matrices, and detailed modality/fusion and cross-subject/action case studies in Figures 10–15. Section 10.3 also reports a TokenHMR fine-tuning comparison. These substantially expand diagnostics beyond v1's scaling analysis and limited mesh visualizations.

E5.justification: Figure 13 newly reports per-action MVE distributions using box-and-whisker plots. This adds error-variability reporting, although the whisker convention is unspecified. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds extensive joint, rotation, translation, and parameter-count results; supplementary figures add action, distance, and HAR findings. Table 3 revises S1 RPC MVE/MJE/MRE/TE from 89.5/76.6/9.2/48.6 to 90.4/77.5/9.3/49.4, although Table 6 retains the earlier values. Section 8 additionally reports loading time decreasing from over 18 to under 1 hour per epoch.

T1.justification: Sections 10.2–10.3 newly provide explicit mathematical definitions of the combined localization/mesh objective and component losses, plus crop-to-full-image and translation equations. v1 only sketches these components. No new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The largest-dataset and first RT-based HMR claims remain. The introduction's benchmark contribution and Section 4 now claim demonstrated downstream human motion prediction alongside HAR, broadening the claimed contribution without corresponding results in the supplied supplement.

C2.justification: The supplement adds specific limitations: unstable body-shape estimates attributed to weak appearance/geometric cues, reduced accuracy at close and distant ranges, and possible misuse for behavior monitoring. These refine applicability and failure explanations while retaining the main interpretations of radar, fusion, and generalization.

D1.justification: v3 supplies dataset organization, sparse compression and LMDB loading instructions, the full action list, training hyperparameters, hardware, training time, crop dimensions, preprocessing, and HAR implementation details. Its abstract replaces the future-release promise with a public-access statement and link. These substantially address information missing from v1.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 52 to 72 entries, adding robotics, retargeting, imitation, radar motion prediction, and implementation references. The introduction strengthens robotics positioning, but the central comparison with existing radar datasets and the RT-based HMR novelty argument remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets are extensively rewritten. A structured supplement adds substantial exposition of existing data organization, action design, implementation, applications, and diagnostic interpretation. The main section sequence remains, but explanatory coverage and document organization expand considerably.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 7–15 and Tables 5–6, covering data organization, loading, actions, detailed results, and diagnostics. It also revises the overview/system illustrations and redraws Figure 5 with changed axes, legends, and removal of numerical bar labels.

improvement.justification: v1 refers to implementation details in an absent supplement; v3 supplies substantial training, loss, preprocessing, hardware, and dataset-access documentation. Detailed results and action/distance diagnostics also make the benchmark more assessable and usable. These resolve an important documentation deficiency. The gains remain substantial despite inconsistent values between Tables 3 and 6, conflicting sensing-range descriptions, and the unsupported motion-prediction claim.
